## Natural history notes

A small pyramid ant characterized by its slender dark brown to black body, long legs, and raised hump-like profile on the thorax that gives it the “hump-backed” appearance. In Florida, it is associated with sandy open habitats, especially sandhills, open pinewoods, scrub edges, trails, and lightly disturbed sandy ground where colonies can nest in soil. It forages actively on the ground for small insects, dead arthropods, nectar, honeydew, and other sugary resources, while its nests and foraging activity help move nutrients through sandy soils and provide prey for other insect-eating wildlife.
